svg.title: From central triviality to an inner canonical extension
svg.desc: For a separable AFD type III zero factor, finite orbit partitions first identify the module with a constant flow translation. Removing that translation leaves trace multiplier exp(t zero). Finite-class transport of one nontrivial phase would give a displaced centralizing unitary sequence, a contradiction. The return automorphism is therefore inner, the multiplier equals one, and a height-strip construction gives the core implementer.
svg.text: Central triviality and the core-inner kernel
M: separable AFD type III₀ factor · b: canonical extension · δ: dual flow
1. Finite partitions detect the center action
Different flow orbits have different finite-class roots at every stage.
ν(E) > 0 ⇒ choose colors with ‖b(fₙ) − fₙ‖²₂,ν ≥ ν(E)/4
But the fₙ are asymptotically flow invariant, hence centralizing in the crossing.
Central triviality ⇒ S preserves flow orbits ⇒ S = Ft₀ (CTK.7–12)

c = b δ−t₀ ⇒ τ c = et₀τ ⇒ ν a = et₀ν in A = N ⋊β ℤ
If the fibers aₓ are non-inner, one fixed phase z ≠ 1 works almost everywhere.

3. The phase contradiction gives the core implementer
wₙ centralizing in A ⇒ ‖(z − 1)wₙ‖Φ,# → 0, but it equals √2 |z − 1|.
Therefore a = Ad(v) ⇒ et₀ = 1 ⇒ t₀ = 0. (CTK.25–26)
For G(x,r) = (Tx,r − H(x)), the strip 0 ≤ r < H(x) meets each orbit once.
Extend W from that strip by W(Gξ) = d(pₓ(Gξ))W(ξ), with H = −log h > 0.
γ̃ = Ad(vW) ⇒ α̃ is inner after removing the type-I tensor factor. (CTK.27–30)
